title: ARSIA DORA Incident Event Payload
description: Validates the payload object of a DORA incident event message (ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2). Generated when an infrastructure failure occurs during a financial operation — provider timeout, network error, database failure, broker relay failure, or TLS handshake failure. The payload feeds into the operator's DORA (Regulation 2022/2554/EU) incident classification and reporting process per Articles 17-19. Business logic failures (insufficient funds, compliance rejection, etc.) do NOT trigger DORA incidents per §6.2.1.

type.description: Payload type identifier for DORA incident events. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

data.description: DORA incident report data fields. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

incident_type.description: Classifies the nature of the ICT-related incident per DORA Article 17(1). Infrastructure failures only — business logic failures do not trigger DORA incidents (§6.2.1). Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

affected_service.description: The agent-id of the component that failed. For provider timeouts, the provider's agent-id; for database failures, the agent's own agent-id; for broker failures, the broker's agent-id. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

started_at.description: When the incident was first detected — typically the timestamp of the first failed operation. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

resolved_at.description: When the incident was resolved. Null or absent if the incident is ongoing. A subsequent event with the same original_payment_reference and non-null resolved_at SHOULD be sent when resolved. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

estimated_impact.description: Human-readable description of estimated impact. SHOULD include number of affected transfers, estimated financial impact, services affected, and geographic scope. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

severity.description: Severity classification of the incident. low: transient single-transfer failure, retry expected. medium: persistent multi-transfer or high-value failure. high: sustained outage of critical service. critical: total loss of payment processing capability. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.

original_payment_reference.description: The payment_reference of the transfer that triggered the incident detection. Links the DORA incident event to the MiFID II audit trail for correlation. Per ARSIA-Assets.md §6.2.2.
